Cultural Events in Kathmandu

Kathmandu is a living cultural capital. From centuries-old Newari festivals in Patan Durbar Square to modern theatre productions at Mandala, Shilpee, and Theatre Village, the valley's cultural pulse is strong year-round.

Browse upcoming plays, dance performances, poetry readings, heritage walks, traditional festivals, and film screenings. Whether you're a local looking to rediscover your roots or a visitor wanting to experience Nepal beyond the trekking routes, this is where to start.

Most cultural events are intimate — seats are limited, book ahead.

Frequently asked questions

What are the biggest cultural festivals in Kathmandu?+–

Indra Jatra, Dashain, Tihar, Holi, and the Rato Machhindranath Jatra are among the largest. Kata Jaam? also features modern theatre festivals, dance showcases, and multicultural events throughout the year.

Where can I watch Nepali theatre in Kathmandu?+–

Mandala Theatre in Anamnagar, Shilpee Theatre in Battisputali, and Theatre Village in Lazimpat host regular productions in Nepali and English.

Do I need to book cultural events in advance?+–

Yes — venues are often small (50-200 seats) and popular productions sell out quickly. Use Kata Jaam? to RSVP or buy tickets early.
